about.title: About me
about.text: I work on the same kind of thing almost every time: systems a business runs on every day. I built the payment-allocation engine for a wholesale distributor —post-dated checks, discounts, refinancing plans—, a POS that keeps selling when the internet drops, and multi-tenant setups serving several clients from a single codebase. Before I write a line, I take the time to understand how the business works; for me that's half the job.

dma.title: Distribuidora DMA
dma.short: A production B2B platform for a wholesale automotive parts distributor in Argentina — full commercial lifecycle from catalog and orders through payment processing, collections, and CRM.
highlights: Payment allocation engine: sequential document settlement (oldest-first), DCR-based discount rates, check interest amortization, and multi-installment refinancing plan generation
43 RTK Query API slices for server state, React Context for session state, and a multi-tenant config system enabling white-label deployment per distributor
50+ NestJS modules with JWT RBAC (Admin/Seller/Customer roles), ERP sync via multisoft_id, GPS customer visit tracking, and PDF/Excel export

media.coverAlt: DMA B2B distribution platform — main dashboard
gallery: Dashboard with sales statistics and seller targets
Payment allocation engine — document settlement view

context.title: Project context
context.callout: Argentine wholesale distribution runs on complex credit workflows — post-dated checks, discount rates tied to document age, and refinancing plans — that no generic ERP handles cleanly at the point of sale.
p: The distributor's sales force needed a field tool — on mobile or desktop — to quote, place orders, register multi-method payments, and track client balances in real time, operating alongside the existing ERP (Multisoft).

The platform covers the full commercial lifecycle: product catalog with vehicle compatibility matrices, sales orders, open invoice tracking, multi-method payment processing with check interest calculation, collection workflow, and a seller-facing CRM.

built.title: What I built
b: Payment allocation engine: per-value sequential settlement of open invoices (oldest first), DCR-based discount rate computation, check interest amortization (annual rate → daily → deferred days), and PlanCalculator for multi-installment refinancing schedules

Full-stack architecture: Next.js 15 frontend with 43 RTK Query API slices and React Context for session state, backed by a 50+ module NestJS REST API on MongoDB Atlas with JWT authentication and role-based access control

Multi-tenant config system enabling white-label deployment per distributor via environment variables, per-client theming, and feature flags (Maps, Finance, CRM, Marketing) — no code changes required per new client
built.note: In production, used daily by the sales force of a real wholesale distributor: 520+ clients and an 11,000+ product catalog per distributor. Includes GPS customer visit tracking, Excel/PDF export, i18n, Recharts dashboards, and a mobile-first interface for field sellers.

nova.title: Nõva Sushi
nova.short: Marketing site and franchise-acquisition funnel for Nõva Sushi, the 3-location restaurant group I co-founded — a digital sales tool for consumers and franchise investors.

facts.role: Co-founder & Head of Technology (Next.js 15 + Framer Motion)

highlights: Conversion-focused site with a franchise funnel (ROI modeling, real operational KPIs, WhatsApp-powered lead capture), handling 3,000 online orders per month
Interactive menu showcase with 100+ items, real-time search, and keyboard-accessible modals
Scroll-driven animation system using Framer Motion (useScroll, useTransform, AnimatePresence)

gallery: Interactive menu showcase with category filters
media.solutionAlt: Franchise investor funnel and lead capture

problem.title: The project
problem.callout: Most restaurant websites are passive pages. This one was built as an active digital sales tool with two parallel conversion funnels.
p: Nova Sushi needed more than a menu and a contact form — a digital presence that could attract customers and convert entrepreneurs into franchise partners simultaneously.

The result is a statically-generated Next.js 15 site with two flows: a consumer journey centered on the brand story and menu, and a full franchise acquisition funnel featuring real operational KPIs, investment formats, ROI scenario modeling, and a structured lead capture process.

solution.title: What I built
b: Full franchise acquisition funnel across 10 sections — differentiators, real KPIs, 3 ROI scenarios, onboarding process, and WhatsApp-powered lead capture
Interactive product catalog with real-time category filtering and text search over 100+ items, integrated with AWS S3 as image CDN
Scroll-driven animation system using Framer Motion's useScroll and useTransform hooks, with AnimatePresence for modal mount/unmount transitions
solution.note: Deployed to Vercel with production SEO: JSON-LD structured data (Restaurant, Breadcrumb, and FAQ schemas), dynamic sitemap/robots generation, and full Open Graph coverage.

gourmetify.title: Gourmetify
gourmetify.short: A production-grade multi-tenant SaaS platform that replaces the entire operational stack of a restaurant — inventory, POS, orders, procurement, HR, and financial reporting in a single application.
highlights: Offline-first POS with IndexedDB mutation queuing, UUID-based server idempotency, and automatic sync with exponential backoff
Dual payment-provider integration (Stripe + MercadoPago): SaaS subscription billing (B2B) and in-restaurant customer payments (B2C), both with atomic webhook idempotency
Bill-of-materials costing engine with wastage factors, 40+ model multi-tenant schema, and 3-tier plan feature gating across 140+ API routes

gallery: Offline-first POS with sync status indicator
Kanban order management with kitchen display
media.problemAlt: Restaurant operational chaos in Latin America

problem.title: The problem
problem.callout: The average restaurant in Latin America runs on WhatsApp groups, notebooks, and spreadsheets — with no real visibility into food cost, cash flow, or profitability.
p: Restaurant owners don't know their real food cost, can't track ingredient waste, have no daily P&L visibility, and manage staff with paper attendance sheets. Every operational pain is a manual process.

Existing solutions are either enterprise-grade and unaffordable, or single-purpose tools that don't integrate. Gourmetify replaces the entire stack with one affordable SaaS platform built for the realities of Latin American food service.

built.title: What I built
b: Multi-tenant PostgreSQL architecture with explicit row isolation across 40+ models, 5-role RBAC, and a centralized feature-flag system enforced across 140+ API route handlers

Offline-first POS using IndexedDB for mutation queuing, server-side UUID deduplication for idempotent sale submission, and automatic retry with exponential backoff — sales are never lost during outages

Dual payment-provider integration: Stripe for SaaS subscription billing (with automated grace-period and downgrade flows) and MercadoPago for in-restaurant customer payments — both with atomic webhook idempotency via a claimed-event table
built.note: In production with 5 active venues (including Nõva Sushi's 3 locations), processing 1,000+ tickets/month per venue. The platform spans 30+ operational modules: inventory with BOM recipe costing, Kanban order management with kitchen display, supplier procurement, employee attendance with PIN time clock, and automated financial reporting via email.

gourmetify.summary: B2B SaaS point-of-sale (POS) and management platform for the food service industry.
b: Live in production across 5 venues (including Nõva Sushi's 3 locations), processing 1,000+ monthly tickets per venue.
Offline-first POS using IndexedDB for local persistence and background sync upon reconnection.
Multi-tenant architecture with Next.js 16, TypeScript and PostgreSQL, with per-tenant data isolation.
